entities.name: PMID:25443366
observations: 2014 study titled “Gastroprotective effect of the iridoid fraction from Barleria prionitis leaves on experimentally-induced gastric ulceration.”

entities.name: Barleria iridoid fraction
observations: Standardized iridoid fraction from Barleria prionitis leaves, administered orally at 50, 100, or 200 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days in rats.

entities.name: Experimental gastric ulceration
observations: In rat models induced by aspirin, ethanol, cold-restraint stress, and pylorus ligation, the fraction reduced ulceration in a dose-dependent manner; reported protection ranges were 18.67–66.26%, 24.65–63.25%, 20.77–59.42%, and 16.93–77.04%, respectively.

entities.name: BPE gastroprotection
observations: The fraction decreased acid-pepsin secretion and increased mucin and mucosal glycoproteins in pylorus-ligated rats.
Cold-restraint experiments showed reduced ulcer index and lipid peroxidation, with increased catalase activity; reported statistical significance was P<0.01–0.001.
The study authors concluded that the fraction has anti-ulcerogenic and antioxidant potential.
